sections.title: What one has to do
sections.content: You know *kell* as "is needed": *Több szék kell.* Put an infinitive in front of it and it says what one has to do: *Fizetni kell.* (One has to pay.) *Várni kell.* (One has to wait.) It is a general statement with no person: *kell* never changes, and the infinitive has no ending.

sections.title: Kell + infinitive
rows: One has to book a table.
There is no need to wait.

sections.title: Where the -t goes
sections.content: The dish or thing belongs to the infinitive, so it keeps its *-t*: *Asztalt kell foglalni.* With only a noun and *kell* there is no *-t*: *Egy asztal kell.* (A table is needed.)

items.english: One has to book a table.
There is no need to pay.

sections.content: *Nem kell* means "there is no need", not "you must not". And do not put a person on *kell*: it is *Fizetni kell*, whoever pays.
